name: observed-command-exits
goal: Commands that exit during synchronous spawn observers retain exit and output events in Node and Bun without holding resource reservations

evidence: New synchronous PID observer from d13fc5e7 can consume Bun child exit events before runIsolated attaches its exit listener; native Bun sh exits normally at zero observer delay and falsely times out at 100 ms. Linux timeout relies on that missing exit event.

Existing process-runner tests execute under Node and observe only a cheap callback. Extend their normal exit/output case with native Bun at zero and delayed observer delivery; no unrelated broad suite needed.
/tmp/harness-observed-exit-red.log: unchanged standardized native Bun matrix passes 0 ms and fails 100 ms, receiving timeout/null/true instead of passed/0/false in 3.89 seconds.

Register child exit listeners before invoking synchronous observers. Keep the native runtime/observer matrix in the existing process-runner suite and require lifecycle boundary tests when extending observers.
Child exit listener installed before onSpawn; standard Node/Bun exit-output matrix covers synchronous observer delay, with a matching AGENTS.md review checkpoint.
/tmp/harness-observed-exit-green.log: all 6 process-runner cases pass; final Node/Bun matrix with real stdout/stderr also passes in isolated restored source.
/tmp/harness-observed-guard-red.log rejects old HEAD source with timeout/null/true; /tmp/harness-observed-guard-green.log passes the same unchanged matrix after restoring repaired source.
